title: Customers and CX
hired_for: To keep the customers we already paid to win: fix what makes them contact us, return or leave, and know which customers actually make money.

jobs.job: Get first-time buyers to order a second time
jobs.why: Most first buyers never come back, so every new customer costs full price to win. If the second order does not happen, ad costs eat the profit.

watch.metric: second order rate within 90 days of the first order, by month of first order
watch.source: Shopify orders

drives.metric: gross profit per customer at 180 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 18% of January buyers ordered again within 90 days. After: a fixed post-purchase path lifts the April cohort to 23%.

jobs.job: Cut the 'where is my order' messages
jobs.why: Order status questions are often the biggest share of support contacts. Each one costs money to answer and tells you the buyer is worried.

watch.metric: delivery status tickets per 100 orders, 30 day
watch.source: Gorgias tickets joined to Shopify orders

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 9 status tickets per 100 orders. After: 3 proactive shipping updates and a branded tracking page bring it under 5 within 30 days.

jobs.job: Turn more returns into exchanges or store credit, and refund fast
jobs.why: A refund loses the sale. An exchange keeps it. Slow refunds cause angry tickets and chargebacks.

watch.metric: share of returned value kept as an exchange or store credit, 30 day
watch.source: returns app (Loop, AfterShip Returns) or Shopify returns

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 12% of return value is kept, refunds take 9 days. After: exchange-first returns keep 30% and refunds land in 4 days.

jobs.job: Know which customers make money after returns, shipping, support and discounts
jobs.why: Revenue per customer hides the ones who return half their orders or only buy on deep discount. Without profit per customer you cannot tell who is worth winning.

watch.metric: gross profit per customer at 180 days, by acquisition channel
watch.source: Shopify orders and refunds, product costs, Gorgias tickets

drives.metric: most you can pay to win a new customer, by channel

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: only revenue per customer is known. After: Meta buyers show $41 profit at 180 days, discount-code buyers show $9.

jobs.job: Answer customers fast and solve it the first time
jobs.why: Slow or repeated replies turn a small problem into a refund, a bad review or a lost customer.

watch.metric: median first reply time in hours, 7 day
watch.source: Gorgias

drives.metric: support satisfaction score after a ticket, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: median first reply is 14 hours. After: saved replies and a staffed morning block bring it to 3 hours within 2 weeks.

jobs.job: Answer bad reviews and collect more honest reviews at the right moment
jobs.why: Unanswered bad reviews scare off new buyers. Too few recent reviews make good products look risky.

watch.metric: new reviews per 100 delivered orders, and share of 1 to 2 star reviews answered within 5 days, 30 day
watch.source: reviews app (Judge.me, Okendo, Yotpo)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 reviews per 100 orders, 40% of bad reviews answered. After: a review ask timed to delivery plus 2 days gives 5 per 100, and all bad reviews get a reply.

jobs.job: Cut returns caused by wrong size or wrong expectation
jobs.why: Returns cost 2 shipping legs, handling, and often the product. Many come from a product page or a first week that set the wrong expectation.

watch.metric: return rate by product and return reason, 60 day
watch.source: Shopify returns or returns app reasons

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 14% of units come back, half tagged 'too small'. After: a fit guide and a first-week how-to email bring it to 10% on that product.

jobs.job: Win back customers who are drifting away, before a discount
jobs.why: Customers past their normal reorder time slip away quietly. Catching them early costs less than a new customer.

watch.metric: share of lapsed customers who order again within 60 days
watch.source: Shopify orders and Klaviyo

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1,200 customers are past 1.5x their usual reorder gap with no contact. After: a win-back series brings 7% back in 60 days.

jobs.job: Keep chargebacks below the card network limit
jobs.why: Disputes cost the order, the fee and the fight. Above about 1% of orders, the payment processor can hold funds or close the account.

watch.metric: chargeback rate, 30 day
watch.source: Shopify Payments or Stripe disputes

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 0.8% and rising after a slow-refund month. After: faster refunds and clear billing names bring it to 0.3% within 60 days.

jobs.job: Stop paying ads to reach people who already buy anyway
jobs.why: Ad platforms happily count sales from existing customers who would have bought anyway. That spend looks good and earns little.

watch.metric: share of Meta purchases from existing customers, and cost per returning purchase, 30 day
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager and Shopify customer list

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 35% of Meta purchases are returning buyers at $28 each. After: past buyers excluded from prospecting, cost per new customer falls 12%.

jobs.job: Find the worst moment after purchase and fix it before paying for extras
jobs.why: One broken promise, like a late parcel or a hard return, outweighs any gift in the box. Fix the low point first.

watch.metric: share of bad reviews and tickets tied to one step after purchase, 30 day (proxy: tagged reasons)
watch.source: Gorgias tags and reviews app

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 40% of complaints name delivery delays. After: a real delivery date on the product page cuts that to 20% in 30 days.

jobs.job: Turn a bad experience into a loyal customer
jobs.why: Customers whose problem was fixed well often buy again more than those with no problem. A cold, slow fix loses them for good.

watch.metric: second order rate of customers who had a problem ticket versus those who did not, 180 day
watch.source: Gorgias tickets joined to Shopify orders

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: customers with a problem reorder at 11% versus 19%. After: agents can make a one-time exception and the gap closes to 16% versus 19%.

jobs.job: Learn what people contact us about and fix the cause
jobs.why: Tickets tell you what is broken on the site, in the box or in delivery. If no one reads them by reason, the same problem costs money every week.

watch.metric: share of tickets by top 5 reasons, 30 day
watch.source: Gorgias ticket tags

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 'discount code did not work' is 15% of tickets. After: the checkout fix drops it to 2% the next month.

jobs.job: Let software answer the simple questions and keep people for the hard ones
jobs.why: Staff time goes to copy-paste answers while upset customers wait. Automating the simple ones frees people for cases that need judgement.

watch.metric: share of tickets resolved without a person, and their satisfaction score, 30 day
watch.source: Gorgias

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 5% resolved automatically. After: order status and return-start questions automated, 30% resolved with satisfaction held above 85%.

jobs.job: Promise a delivery date we can actually hit
jobs.why: A vague or wrong delivery estimate creates worry, status tickets and refund requests. A real date, slightly padded, builds trust.

watch.metric: share of orders delivered by the date shown to the buyer, 30 day
watch.source: Shopify fulfilment events and carrier tracking (AfterShip, ShipStation)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 78% arrive by the shown date. After: estimates built from real carrier times reach 92%.

jobs.job: Set clear limits on what the AI support agent can refund or promise
jobs.why: An AI agent that refunds or promises too much costs real money, and one that promises the wrong thing costs trust.

watch.metric: AI agent actions above their set limit, count, and AI-closed tickets reopened, 30 day
watch.source: Gorgias AI agent log

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no limit is written down, 6 refunds above $50 went out last month. After: a $30 cap with a human hand-off, 0 over-limit actions.

jobs.job: Measure satisfaction and learn why it moves
jobs.why: Without a steady score and the reasons behind it, the team argues from opinions. A falling score warns you before repeat rate drops.

watch.metric: satisfaction score after a ticket, 30 day, and net promoter score, quarterly
watch.source: Gorgias survey and a post-purchase survey app

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: satisfaction is not collected. After: 82% satisfied, with 'slow refund' as the top reason for low scores.

jobs.job: Show the same good rating everywhere we sell
jobs.why: A product rated 4.7 on site and 3.9 on Amazon loses the marketplace sale. Buyers check more than one place.

watch.metric: star rating per product on site versus each marketplace, 90 day
watch.source: reviews app and marketplace seller tools (Amazon Seller Central, Walmart Seller Center)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: hero product is 4.8 on site and 4.1 on Amazon, driven by 'thin fabric' reviews. After: a listing fix and replies lift it to 4.4 in 90 days.

jobs.job: Treat the best customers well without training them to wait for discounts
jobs.why: The top 20% of customers often bring half the profit. Discounting them teaches them to wait; ignoring them lets them drift.

watch.metric: repeat rate and gross profit of the top 20% of customers, 365 day
watch.source: Shopify orders and product costs

drives.metric: share of gross profit from the top 20% of customers

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: VIPs get the same 20% codes as everyone. After: early access instead of discounts keeps their repeat rate at 60% with 8 points more margin.

jobs.job: Spend on a loyalty program only if it changes buying
jobs.why: Points programs often reward people who would have bought anyway. Keep it only if members buy more often than similar non-members.

watch.metric: repeat rate of reward redeemers versus similar non-redeemers, 180 day
watch.source: loyalty app (Smile, Yotpo Loyalty) and Shopify orders

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the program costs $2,000 a month with no read. After: redeemers repeat at 26% versus 24% for similar buyers, so the cost is cut in half.

jobs.job: Spot serial returners and refund abuse
jobs.why: A small group of customers can cause a large share of refunds. Left alone, they drag down margin and make every return policy look too generous.

watch.metric: share of refund value from customers with 3 or more returns in 180 days
watch.source: Shopify orders and returns

drives.metric: refund cost as a share of revenue

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2% of customers cause 18% of refund value. After: flagged accounts lose free returns and refund value falls 10%.

jobs.job: Spend on packaging and inserts only where it pays back
jobs.why: Nice boxes and gifts cost money on every order. Keep only what brings reviews, posts or repeat orders.

watch.metric: packaging and insert cost per order, and unboxing posts or reviews that mention packaging per 100 orders, 90 day (proxy)
watch.source: product costs and reviews app

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $2.40 per order on inserts with no read. After: a 60-day split test shows no repeat gain, cost cut to $0.90.

jobs.job: Keep one record per real customer
jobs.why: The same person as a guest checkout, an email subscriber and an Amazon buyer looks like 3 new customers. Repeat rate and profit per customer come out wrong.

watch.metric: share of orders matched to one customer profile across store, email and marketplace
watch.source: Shopify customers, Klaviyo profiles, marketplace orders

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 71% of orders match one profile. After: merging by email and phone reaches 92%, and the true repeat rate reads 3 points higher.

jobs.job: Answer customer privacy requests on time
jobs.why: US state privacy laws give a deadline (45 days under California law) to delete or share a person's data. Missing it risks fines and complaints.

watch.metric: share of privacy requests closed before the legal deadline
watch.source: brand brain privacy request log (manual, no platform report)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: requests sit in the support inbox with no clock. After: every request is logged with a due date, 100% closed on time.

jobs.job: Match every refund to its sales tax adjustment
jobs.why: Refunds that are not reflected in the sales tax filing mean paying tax on money you gave back, or a mismatch in an audit.

watch.metric: share of completed refunds with a matching tax adjustment, per filing period
watch.source: Shopify refunds and the tax tool (Avalara, TaxJar)

drives.metric: sales tax overpaid on refunded orders

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: unknown. After: 98% of refunds match, and $1,100 of overpaid tax is claimed back.
